messages.subject: comments in sample output
parts:
I added comments to the beginning of the sample
CSV format laying out the command arguments used
to call Stan.

If you're using R's read.csv() you'll need an
extra argument:

comment.char="#"

I chose the usual csv comment char, which I hope
is OK.

The output now looks like:

# Samples Generated by Stan
#
# stan_version_major=alpha
# stan_version_minor=0
# data=
# init=random initialization
# append_samples=0
# seed=1330119571
# chain_id=1
# iter=2000
# warmup=1000
# thin=1
# leapfrog_steps=-1
# epsilon=-1
# epsilon_pm=0
# delta=0.5
# gamma=0.05
#
lp__,y
-0.00825633,-21.285
-0.00825633,-21.285
-0.00825633,-21.285

I'm hoping we'll be able to parse out the comments in R.
Any comment line with an "=" sign is for a key/value pair.
Note that some are blank, as in this run didn't involve a data
file or an init file.

I could get rid of the "Samples Generated by" and blank
lines if that makes a difference.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: comments in sample output
parts:
On Feb 24, 4:48 pm, Bob Carpenter <c...@alias-i.com> wrote:
> I added comments to the beginning of the sample
> CSV format laying out the command arguments used
> to call Stan.
>
> If you're using R's read.csv() you'll need an
> extra argument:
>
>    comment.char="#"

That should be fine for R. I think it will be slightly faster to
instead not specify comment.char and to instead specify skip = 18
(assuming there are always 18 extra lines at the top), like

read.csv("samples.csv", skip = 18)

That way R just ignores the first 18 lines and does not waste time
scanning each additional line for a #.

I suppose in the future there may be more than 18 lines to skip, in
which case maybe one of the commented lines should give the
appropriate R call?

Ben
